strings.obs.berlin.window.text: Above the snow-covered roofs of the tenements, the dome of the Great Hall stands in the haze, so far off that it looks more like a change in the weather than a building. In the department they say every line we draw contributes to it. Across the street, light burns in only a few windows; the other flats count, as the notices put it, as vacated. The flag on the façade has hung there since the last holiday. After a few days you stop seeing it, just as you stop seeing the gutters.
strings.obs.berlin.notice.text: A typewritten list of names, house numbers and floors, each line followed by the word “relocated” and a date from this autumn. The column for the new address has been left empty throughout – presumably it will be filled in once the responsible office has completed its records. I know two of the addresses; they lie exactly where the new axis runs on our plans.
strings.obs.berlin.photo.text: The department photograph from the summer of 1961, taken in front of the model of the Hall, everyone in shirtsleeves. Someone has scratched out Herr Brandt’s face with a pin, carefully, until only white paper was left. His drawing table has been covered since the spring. We were told he had been transferred, and, like everyone else, I did not ask where.
